text:
alex: Heads-up — after rolling CUDA driver 535.x -> 545.x on staging last night, autotuner is picking a different kernel path for short sequences and p99 latency for our chat route jumped ~18%.

maria: Ugh. Seen anything in the perf traces?

alex: Ran a quick profiling capture. Key observations: kernel hitrate for the fused-attn path dropped from ~92% -> ~57% on A100-like profiles. KV cache hit distribution shifted (more misses for seq<=64). I pasted the flamegraph gist: https://internal.gists/7f3a

ryan: deploy-bot shows the driver upgrade deployed to staging at 03:12 UTC: 
deploy-bot: "driver-upgrade: cuda-545.12 applied to pool `staging-rt`"

alex: Here's the perf snippet I shared in case useful:
```
# perf sample (aggregated)
fused_attn_kernel_v2: 57.1% (was 92.4%)
fallback_block_attn: 39.8% (was 6.8%)
kv-cache-lookup: miss-rate increased 3.6x for seq<=64
end-to-end p99: 220ms -> 260ms
```

maria: Sounds like a kernel-selection heuristic change in the driver or cuBLAS that impacts our autotuner feedback loop. Did autotune logs show different feature inputs?

alex: Yes — autotune scoring bumped the latency estimate for the fused path because measured kernel micro-benchmarks returned worse cycle counts for short sequences. The autotuner then favored the block-attn path.

ryan: Could be a kernel codepath regression in CUDA or different launch heuristics on that driver. We saw similar patterns historically when kernel occupancy heuristics changed.

sre-jen: What's the rollback plan? We need SLA-safe options for prod if this hits there.

alex: Proposed steps:
1) Pin staging + canary prod nodes to previous driver (rollback to 535.x) to verify reversion of hitrate.
2) Add a temporary autotune override: force fused-attn for seq<=64 on G5/H100/A100 families (config flag).
3) Collect detailed microbenchmarks (per-arch, per-batch) and send to NVIDIA if confirmed.
4) Create a targeted canary with traffic steering (5% traffic) and increased observability.

maria: For (2) what's the config flag schema? Something like `runtime.autotune.force_kernel_map`?

alex: Yeah. We can do: `runtime.autotune.override = {"kernel_hint": "fused_attn_v2", "max_seq": 64, "reason": "post-driver-hitrate-drop"}`. It is hot-reloadable.

ryan: Also add a metric we don't currently emit: `kernel_hitrate_by_seq_bucket` (seq=1-16,17-32,33-64,65-128) per model-version. That will help track regressions and auto-alert.

perf-bot: New metric request created: MET-1287 kernel_hitrate_by_seq_bucket. Alert rule option: p99-drop or absolute hitrate < 70% for 10m.

sre-jen: For rollback, can infra do a targeted driver pin for affected instance groups? I don't want a full cluster rollback unless necessary.

ryan: Yes — we can pin driver at nodepool level. Steps: `rdctl nodepool update --name=staging-rt --driver-version=535.79`. For prod, create a canary nodepool `prod-rt-canary` pinned to 535 and route 3-5% traffic.

maria: If we force the fused path while investigating, we should add a circuit-breaker: if p99 worsens further, revert to autotune. No point making it worse.

alex: Agreed. I'll prepare the override and a rollback playbook:
- roll-forward: apply override -> monitor 30m -> if p99 reduces and kernel_hitrate recovers, expand rollout.
- roll-back: remove override -> pin driver back to 535 -> rollback traffic routing to pre-upgrade pools.

sre-jen: Add runbook steps for support: how to check kernel hitrate (one-liner), how to apply hot override, and who to page.

alex: One-liner to fetch recent histograms (internal):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://obs.redwood.example/api/metrics/query?q=kernel_hitrate_by_seq_bucket&model=chat-v2&range=15m
```

maria: OK I'll open a support ticket with NVIDIA and attach the microbench logs. Attach the autotuner logs too.

ryan: I'm going to stage the canary pin + 5% traffic route in the morning. Alex — please paste the override payload when ready and I'll apply it.

alex: Will do. I'll also add the metric to the per-route dashboard so product can watch.

sre-jen: Thanks. If anyone sees this in prod, page SRE on call and follow the runbook. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — nice narrow plan. Let's regroup after the canary runs and the metric shows trending.

alex: Filed follow-ups: PERF-4553 (microbench corpus), SRE-4554 (canary rollout), AUTOTUNE-998 (override flag).
